best_for: People who already run a Plex Media Server, or watch from a friend's, and want a desktop player with better playback and offline downloads than the browser app.
description:
Plex is the desktop app from Plex, Inc. for watching your own movies and shows, along with what Plex offers on top. On the server side, Plex Media Server scans your files and sorts them into a library on its own.

In the app your videos show up with posters, ratings, cast lists and season and episode details that Plex adds for you. You can browse more than 600 free live TV channels, rent new movies, and keep a watchlist. Plex also has a social side: you can find friends, follow other fans and read their reviews.

points.title: A player, not the server
points.text: This app plays media; it does not store or serve your library. For your own movies and shows you also need Plex Media Server running somewhere on your network, and the app talks to it.

points.title: Plays more, and offline
points.text: Plex describes it as the web app's layout with stronger playback and the option to download items to watch offline. Downloads need Plex Media Server 1.16.3 or newer.

points.title: Free at home, paid away
points.text: Streaming across your home network costs nothing. Watching personal video from outside the home needs a Remote Watch Pass (list price USD 2.99 a month or 29.99 a year) or a Plex Pass on your account or the server owner's. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Plex Pass adds the extras
points.text: Downloads, skip intro and credits, hardware transcoding and DVR come with Plex Pass. A new lifetime pass rose to USD 749.99 on July 1, 2026, and a 5-year plan costs USD 249.99. Music and photo streaming to Plexamp and Plex Photos are not subject to the remote fee.

points.title: You sign in with a Plex account
points.text: On first launch the app opens your browser to sign in, then lands on your home page. Plex also offers free ad-supported movies, shows and live TV through the same account.

points.title: Requirements by system
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 or later, 64-bit; the installer is per-machine. macOS needs 10.13 High Sierra or later and ships as one universal build. On Linux, Plex points to Flathub or Snapcraft; the Flatpak is verified as Plex's own and is x64 only.

points.title: Version history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 56 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
